AIM.1.description: run_counter keeps counting past max_on_counts and wraps instead of saturating at the ceiling
AIM.1.reason: If pwm_sync stays high, run_counter wraps to 0 after 2^ON_TIME_W - max_on_counts clocks. It then reads below the ceiling again, so pulse_allowed comes back on and pwm_out goes high again in the middle of the same stuck-high pulse.

AIM.2.description: The envelope is re-armed whenever the gated pulse ends, not only when pwm_sync goes low, so a truncated pulse re-arms while pwm_sync is still high
AIM.2.reason: When pwm_sync stays high for more than max_on_counts+1 clocks, pulse_allowed clears and the next clock takes the low-phase branch, which clears the counter and sets pulse_allowed again. pwm_out drops for one clock and then goes high again, giving the gate driver repeated pulses within one cycle.

AIM.3.description: The saturated-hold branch wins over the low-phase re-arm, so a counter at the ceiling is never cleared
AIM.3.reason: Once one pulse reaches the ceiling, run_counter stays at max_on_counts through the low phase and pulse_allowed stays 0. pwm_out then stays low for every later pulse until max_on_counts goes up.

judgements.reason: If max_on_counts is lowered below run_counter mid-pulse, != stays true, so line 78 keeps counting and pulse_allowed stays 1. The original closes the envelope there.

decisions.reason: ceiling lowered below the elapsed count mid-pulse never tested; reachable in the design via a MAX_ON write during soft start
ceiling lowered below the elapsed count mid-pulse never tested; reachable in the design via a MAX_ON write during soft start

AIM.4.description: The ceiling test is equality instead of less-than, so a ceiling lowered below the running count is missed
AIM.4.reason: If max_on_counts drops below run_counter while pwm_sync is high (soft_start resetting to the floor, or clamping to a lowered max_on_limit), the counter climbs on to wrap-around with pulse_allowed held at 1. pwm_out then follows pwm_sync far past the new ceiling.

AIM.5.description: pulse_allowed is decided from the post-increment count instead of the pre-edge run_counter, which removes the documented +1 clk offset
AIM.5.reason: For any max_on_counts of 1 or more, a pulse longer than the ceiling is cut after max_on_counts clocks instead of max_on_counts+1, so pwm_out's enforced on-time is one clock short.

judgements.reason: On the first low clock after a pulse, run_counter is still nonzero, so pulse_allowed becomes 0. If pwm_sync goes high again after a one-clock low gap, line 125 outputs 0 instead of 1.

decisions.reason: differs only for a one-clock low phase; the 70% analog duty clamp keeps every low phase above 6 clocks

AIM.6.description: The envelope is re-armed only once run_counter has already been cleared, one clock into the low phase, not on its first clock
AIM.6.reason: On the first low clock after a pulse, pulse_allowed goes to 0 while run_counter is still nonzero. If the low phase lasts only one clock (high duty), the next pulse starts with the gate closed, and pwm_out loses that pulse's first clock.

AIM.7.description: run_counter is cleared on the low phase only after a pulse that was truncated, so the on-time of a pulse that ended under the ceiling carries over into the next pulse
AIM.7.reason: After a pwm_sync pulse shorter than max_on_counts, the next pulse starts counting from the previous width, so pwm_out is cut after max_on_counts - W + 1 clocks instead of max_on_counts + 1 (or not cut at all).

judgements.reason: If max is lowered below run_counter, the mutant clamps run_counter down to it. If max is then raised but stays below the original held count, the mutant re-opens at lines 76/79 while the original stays closed.

decisions.reason: differ only if max_on_counts rises during a pulse; soft_start raises it only at pwm_fall, between pulses

AIM.8.description: The saturation branch clamps run_counter to the present ceiling instead of holding it, so a ceiling lowered mid-pulse pulls the elapsed count down to it
AIM.8.reason: If max_on_counts drops below the running count during a high phase and then rises again within the same pulse (still at or below the true elapsed count), the mutant sees run_counter < max_on_counts and re-opens pulse_allowed, so pwm_out gives a second pulse in that cycle. The original keeps the envelope closed.

judgements.reason: With max_on_counts==0 the original takes the else branch (pulse_allowed<=0), but the mutant counts and keeps pulse_allowed=1. The pulse passes through untruncated.

decisions.reason: differs only at a ceiling of 0; the floor is MIN_ON_COUNTS and reg_file clamps MAX_ON to it

AIM.9.description: A zero on-time ceiling is treated as 'no limit', so pulses are passed through untruncated instead of being cut to one clock
AIM.9.reason: With max_on_counts = 0 and pwm_sync high for several clocks, the original pwm_out is high for one clock only (max_on_counts + 1). The mutant passes the whole pulse to pwm_out.

judgements.reason: If max_on_counts drops below run_counter mid-pulse, run_counter != max_on_counts, so pulse_allowed is not cleared and pwm_out stays high where the original truncates.

decisions.reason: ceiling lowered below the elapsed count mid-pulse never tested; reachable in the design via a MAX_ON write during soft start
ceiling lowered below the elapsed count mid-pulse never tested; reachable in the design via a MAX_ON write during soft start

AIM.10.description: The envelope is closed only when the elapsed count equals the ceiling, so the case of a ceiling that has dropped below the elapsed count leaves pulse_allowed open
AIM.10.reason: When max_on_counts falls below run_counter during a pulse (soft_start reloads MIN_ON_CNT on restart, or clamps to max_on_limit), the counter correctly stops but pulse_allowed stays 1, so pwm_out keeps following pwm_sync for the rest of the pulse instead of going low one clock later.

AIM.11.description: The output takes 'pulse in progress' from run_counter being non-zero instead of from pwm_sync, so it follows the counter's one-clock-late view of the pulse
AIM.11.reason: Every untruncated pulse at pwm_out starts and ends one clock later than with pwm_sync gating. A truncated pulse comes out one clock shorter. With a ceiling of 0 the counter never leaves zero, so pwm_out never goes high.
